deficits.evidence: no purpose-built sidewalk, people must walk in the road or on the shoulder
deficits.suggestion: Construct a continuous sidewalk on the left side of the road to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic.

deficits.evidence: the footway is an informal path under 1m and heavily blocked by shops and stalls
deficits.suggestion: Install a proper, unobstructed sidewalk on the right side to provide a safe walking space.

deficits.evidence: shop fronts and stalls extend into the walking area
deficits.suggestion: Implement zoning regulations to ensure shop fronts do not obstruct the pedestrian path.

deficits.evidence: uneven ground and debris along the informal path
deficits.suggestion: Level and pave the right-side pedestrian area to remove trip hazards.

deficits.evidence: high crossing demand due to commercial shops on both sides but no designated crossing facility
deficits.suggestion: Install a marked pedestrian crossing to provide a safe point for people to cross the road.

ratings.reason: The left side lacks a formal sidewalk, though space is limited by the petrol station and buildings.
The right side has an informal, narrow path that does not meet standard footway criteria.
Shop extensions and signage clearly encroach upon the narrow pedestrian area on the right.
The right-side edge is uneven and cluttered with debris and informal structures.
There are no marked crossings despite the high density of commercial activity on both sides.
